title: Statements, questions, requests
goal: Change a statement into a question, a request or an exclamation
intro: There are four kinds of sentences. A statement tells something. A question asks something. A request or order asks someone to do something. An exclamation shows a strong feeling. Each kind has its own word order and its own tone of voice.

rules.rule: A statement: subject first, then the verb.
A question: the helping verb comes before the subject.
examples: Does the train leave at six?

rules.rule: A request starts with the verb. Add “please” or “could you” to make it polite.
An exclamation often starts with “What a…” or “How…”.

mistakes.why: In a question, put the helping verb before the subject.
Use “What a” before a single thing.
Use “What a” before a noun, and “How” before an adjective alone: How nice!

mistakes.right: Could you please take care of this?
mistakes.why: “Do the needful” sounds old and unclear outside India. Say exactly what you need.

ex.y: Use “What a” before a single thing: What a lovely surprise!
“How” goes before an adjective on its own.

ex.q: ___ you send me the file, please?

ex.y: Put the helping verb before the subject.

ex.q: What an amazing idea it is?
ex.fixed: What an amazing idea it is!
ex.y: This is an exclamation, not a question.

ex.fixed: What a beautiful day it is!

ex.a: Could you open the window, please?
ex.y: A polite request: Could you + verb.

ex.q: Make it a question: “She is your sister.”
ex.y: Swap the subject and “is”: Is she your sister?

talk: Imagine you are at a hotel reception. Ask three polite questions and make one request, like “Could you…?”.
